overall: The Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to approve several sets of open and executive session minutes in a timely manner; special meetings count toward the timeliness rule. Minutes already approved, so no further relief ordered.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly failed to approve minutes timely; June 15 open session minutes were approved August 17, and the Board argued special meetings did not count toward the three-meeting limit.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that the Board’s approval on August 17 of the June 15 open session minutes was not timely.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly failed to approve executive session minutes from March, April 2021 timely; the Board argued the spring minutes allegation was untimely.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that the Board’s August 17 approval of the March 2, April 6 and April 20 executive session minutes was also not timely.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
Caution that a future determination of a similar violation may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Board that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
